chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Abī ʿAzzah, who said:

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام passed by me while I was in the fifth circuit of the tawaf, and he said to me: Go along so that we may return here to a man. I said: I am in five circuits; should I complete my seven-circuit tawaf? He said: Cut it short, and preserve it from where you cut it, until you return to the place from which you cut it, then continue upon it.

key_terms.احْفَظْهُ: retain and keep track of the stopping point
key_terms.الشَّوْطِ الْخَامِسِ: the fifth circuit of the tawaf
key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: the ritual circumambulation around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.فَتَبْنِيَ عَلَيْهِ: then resume and continue from that point

ai.seo_question: Can tawaf be interrupted for an excuse and then resumed from where it was stopped?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on interrupting tawaf due to an excuse before completing seven circuits. Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام instructs that the tawaf may be paused, its point of interruption remembered, and then resumed from that exact place upon returning.
